etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin graduātus (“graduated”), from gradus (“step”). Sense 10 of the verb, relating to Japanese entertainment, is a semantic loan from Japanese 卒業 (sotsugyō).

definitions.definition: A person who is recognized by a university as having completed the requirements of a degree studied at the institution.
(US, Canada) A person who is recognized by a high school as having completed the requirements of a course of study at the school.
(Philippines) A person who is recognized as having completed any level of education.
A graduated (marked) cup or other container, thus fit for measuring.
(intransitive, ergative) To be recognized by a school or university as having completed the requirements of a degree studied at the institution.

quote.citation: 2019 February 19, Jeremy Pelzer, “Youngstown School Board member Dario Hunter seeks Green Party presidential nomination”, in cleveland.com‎[1]:
quote.text: After graduating from Princeton University, he earned a law degree in Canada, then worked as an environmental lawyer in Israel before settling on the south side of Youngstown.

definitions.definition: (transitive, proscribed) To be certified as having earned a degree from; to graduate from (an institution).
(transitive) To certify (a student) as having earned a degree
(transitive) To mark (something) with degrees; to divide into regular steps or intervals, as the scale of a thermometer, a scheme of punishment or rewards, etc.

quote.citation: 1852, William Macgillivray, A history of British birds, indigenous and migratory, page 573:
quote.text: As the species graduate into each other, both in form and in habits, from the grass-eating Geese to the fish-eating Harelds, it is difficult,  […]  to divide this large group into sections.

definitions.definition: To prepare gradually; to arrange, temper, or modify by degrees or to a certain degree; to determine the degrees of.

quote.citation: 1650, Thomas Browne, Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  A[braham] Miller, for Edw[ard] Dod and Nath[aniel] Ekins, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Dyers, who advance and graduate their colours with salts.

definitions.definition: (chemistry) To bring to a certain degree of consistency, by evaporation, as a fluid.
(intransitive) To taper, as the tail of certain birds.
(transitive, software engineering) To approve (a feature) for general release.

(intransitive, Japanese entertainment) Of an idol: to exit a group; or of a virtual YouTuber, to leave a management agency; usually accompanied with "graduation ceremony" send-offs, increased focus on the leaving member, and the like.
